ideal: A unit is used exactly when another unit sits in it, a pointer names it, or a tag names it.
note: drop unit_1; 'it' for the repeated unit

ideal: When a test the project does not declare checks a claim, checker reports no untesting for that claim.
note: drop the 'for every' header

ideal: When a run asks for a check command while checker reports any word at all, the run does not exit with code 0.
note: 'any word at all' shows the word is unrelated to the run

ideal: When a conflict cites a unit, checker reports a misnesting for the conflict.
note: drop the 'for every' header

ideal: A fence whose second word is scenario has the role of scenario.
note: condition folded into the subject

ideal:
Checker reports a finding for:
- every unguarded claim, when the project has a runner
- every tag that names no unit
- every adrift test
- every pointer that names no target
- every unit that is neither used nor a conflict
- every unit that a trailer follows
- every document that holds a unit but no index
- every document that holds an index that does not match the document
- every claim that names a site no source holds
- every unit that repeats a unit
note: one shared 'checker reports a finding for' over a list of subjects

ideal: When an expected failure checks neither a bug nor an exception, checker reports an unexplained failure for it.
note: 'neither … nor' for the two negations

ideal: When a bug names an issue that tracker does not know, checker reports a mistracking for the bug.
note: drop the 'for every' header

ideal: When a run asks for a command that is not available, checker reports the command as an unknown command.
note: relative clause instead of a second conjunct

ideal: When document_1 is document_2 without its frontmatter, the two documents hold exactly the same units.
note: two implications said as 'exactly the same units'

ideal: A plugin applies to a document exactly when the document starts with a listing frontmatter that lists the plugin.
note: drop the 'for every' header

ideal: It must be possible that a conflict names two different units and an issue that tracker knows and has not closed, and checker reports no finding for the conflict.
note: one sentence instead of a list of named variables

ideal: When a run asks for a command that is not available, the run exits with code 2.
note: relative clause instead of a second conjunct

ideal: When any frontmatter lists a missing plugin, checker reports that the project lacks that plugin, and every run exits with code 2.
note: 'every run' shows the run is unrelated to the frontmatter

ideal: When a run calls a plugin, checker runs the plugin over every given document.
note: 'every given document' moved to the consequence

ideal: When a document starts with a listing frontmatter that lists a plugin, checker runs the plugin over the document.
note: relative clause instead of a second conjunct

ideal: When a unit repeats a unit, checker reports a rotting for the repeating unit.
note: 'the repeating unit' replaces unit_1

ideal: A run calls a plugin exactly when the run asks for a command the plugin adds and the plugin applies to some document.
note: one sentence instead of a two-item list

ideal: When a document extends another, the other is context for it, and so is every document that is context for the other.
note: 'so is every document' carries the second implication

ideal: A fence whose second word is bounds has the role of bounds.
note: condition folded into the subject

ideal: When a run calls a plugin, the run gets code 0, 1 or 2 from the plugin.

ideal: When any frontmatter lists a missing plugin, every run exits with code 2.
note: 'every run' shows the run is unrelated to the frontmatter

ideal: When the project declares a test that carries no tag, checker reports an uncitation for the test.

ideal: When a run gets code 2 from any plugin, the run exits with code 2.

ideal:
A frontmatter with any of these flaws is a frontmatter that the checker cannot read:
- an entry that starts with an at sign outside quotes
- a key that neither the checker nor a plugin the frontmatter lists defines
- a list that is not closed
- a string that is not closed
- a key that appears twice
- a path that names no document
- an extension that leads back to its own document
- a setting in a document that is not the entry document
note: 'has the flaw of' said once, over a list of flaws

ideal: When a document keeps readings and holds a unit that holds a formula and whose statement is not current, checker reports the statement of the unit.
note: one sentence instead of a four-item list

ideal: Checker does not report an available command as an unknown command.
note: condition folded into the object
